plan.title: mint audit: keep the terminal mint only where it guards a protected store

narratives.Description: mint audit: keep the terminal mint only where it guards a protected store
narratives.Overview:
1. Drop the terminal step. `scope:record-observable-scope` and `scope:record-intent-constraint`, single path and cohort form, no longer call `refuseNonInteractiveMint` and need no `--confirm` or typed phrase; they write from any shell, an agent's included. The UAT refuse stays. The cohort form still prints the frozen set it writes.
2. Declared stamp. These two commands always write `humanApproval: {kind: "declared", actor, mintedAt, mintedVia: <command name>}`. They refuse `--kind` and `--minted-via`. `--actor` is an optional declared-by display field and may name an agent. One local predicate (`declared`, or what `isHumanApprovalStamp` accepts) is used by both builders and both parsers, so legacy human-stamped and `in-harness-ask` records still parse. `isHumanApprovalStamp` is unchanged, so approved-scope, the one-PR proof and every other reader still refuse a declared stamp.
3. Reader with writer. Reader acceptance ships in the same release as the writer. The CHANGELOG says consumers move the pin before writing a declared record, because an older runtime fails the whole record folder on one record it cannot parse.
4. Kept mints. Keep the mint where the record is live authority before any merge: every `authz:*` mutating command and template (including `uat-start`, `uat-suspend`, `revoke` and `one-pr-unit`) and `scope:record-approved-scope`. Add no folder to the protected set.
5. Worker instructions. For these two records, replace "attended ask; unattended park pending a human mint; no parent auto-approve" with "write the declaration with the command and land it on the merge base before the product PR; a declaration is not consent". Keep the operational-versus-invariant classification and the no-soften rule. Files: `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md`; the build, setup and swarm Phase 0 skill text through the skills pack source and render; `content/docs/intent-constraint.md`, `observable-scope.md`, `scope-provenance.md`; `content/commands.md`; `INTENT_CONSTRAINT_REMEDIATION` and `OBSERVABLE_SCOPE_REMEDIATION`; both commands' usage. Mirror consumer-relevant text through agents-entry.
6. One table in `content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md`: every operator-mint command with its store, where the record is read (live hook, local grant store, App store, merge base), whether hooks deny writes inside the checkout, the self-approval it prevents, kept or dropped, and what a kept mint buys (the command stop while agent markers are set, plus the in-checkout write deny). It names the limits: the PowerShell tool (#6981), absolute writes from a linked worktree into the main clone's `.deft/authz/`, forge commits, marker-based presence, and brief stamps checked by shape only (presentation ceiling, durable-effect ceiling). For the two dropped rows it states the control per merge policy: under human merge the stop is the merge that lands the record; under bot merge or a merge under the operator's identity there is none; the story fence refuses direct writes of these paths unless the merge-gate signal is live, and the command is a writer that fence does not see; a fact found mid-build still needs a record PR before the product PR.
7. Tests beside each changed file: each dropped command, single path and cohort, writes its record with agent markers set and no TTY; `--kind` and `--minted-via` are refused; both builders and parsers accept `declared` and legacy records; `isHumanApprovalStamp` rejects `declared`; `scope:record-approved-scope` and one `authz:grant` template still refuse without a TTY.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scope:record-observable-scope` and `scope:record-intent-constraint`, single path and cohort form, write their records from an agent shell with no TTY, `--confirm` or typed phrase, and still refuse during an active UAT lease.
- Records these commands write carry `kind: "declared"` and `mintedVia` naming the command; `--kind` and `--minted-via` are refused on these commands.
- Both builders and both parsers accept `declared` and legacy human-stamped records, and `isHumanApprovalStamp` still rejects `declared`.
- Every `authz:*` mutating command and template and `scope:record-approved-scope` still refuse without the terminal mint.
- The worker preamble, the build, setup and swarm skill text, the record docs, `content/commands.md` and the two remediation strings tell workers to write the declaration and land it before the product PR, not to park for a human mint.
- `content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md` has one table of every operator-mint command with its store, where it is read, hook coverage, what it prevents, kept or dropped, what a kept mint buys, the named limits, and the per-merge-policy control for the two dropped commands.
- Tests cover a dropped command (single and cohort) writing without a TTY under agent markers and a kept command refusing without a TTY.
- The CHANGELOG says the reader ships with the writer and consumers move the pin before writing declared records.
narratives.Constraint:
- Writing today's `operator` stamp, or `mintedVia: in-harness-ask`, from the dropped commands (7080187478 finding 1, 7080179724 finding 3).
- Teaching `isHumanApprovalStamp` about `declared` (7080187478 finding 1, 7080179466 finding 2).
- Parser-only acceptance of `declared` (7080179466 finding 2, 7080187478 finding 1).
- Dropping the terminal call without recutting the worker preamble and skills (7080179466 finding 1, 7080179724 finding 2).
- "Hooks protect the store" as the keep rule, and "agents cannot write the store" as a claim (7080179724 finding 1, 7080179466 finding 3, 7080187478 finding 3).
- Dropping the mint on `authz:uat-start` or `authz:revoke` (7080187478 finding 4, 7080179724 answer 4, 7080179466 answer 4).
- Calling the merge a control without naming the merge policy (7080179724 finding 4, 7080187478 finding 2).
- Adding the two record folders to the protected set (Stop 1 R4; 7080187478 footnote 5).
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/scope-provenance/record-stamp.ts (new): the declared stamp kind, the two declared-writer verbs and one predicate (declared from a declared-writer verb, or what isHumanApprovalStamp accepts). isHumanApprovalStamp stays unchanged.
2. observable-scope/mint.ts and intent-constraint/mint.ts: both builders and both parsers use that predicate.
3. runtime scope-record-observable-scope.ts, scope-record-intent-constraint.ts and scope-record-cohort.ts: no refuseNonInteractiveMint call; always write kind declared with mintedVia = the verb; refuse --kind and --minted-via; --actor optional (declared-by, may be an agent); --confirm accepted and ignored; UAT refusal stays; the cohort still prints the frozen set.
4. Remediation strings, worker preamble, build/setup/swarm skills (pack source, then task packs:render), record docs, content/commands.md: write the declaration with the command and land it before the product PR; a declaration is not consent.
5. content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md: one table of every operator-mint command with store, read-at, hook coverage, what it prevents, kept or dropped, what a kept mint buys, named limits, and the per-merge-policy control for the two dropped commands.
6. Tests: mint-audit.test.ts (dropped verbs write without a TTY under agent markers, single and cohort; kept verbs refuse), record-stamp.test.ts, beside-file tests, and a content-contract test for the docs. Evaluator-surface disclosure, RULE-MAP regenerate, changelog fragment.

## In plain English

Support removing the two terminal stops and labeling new records as declarations. The checked readers cannot establish that a human created those records.

The design needs one substantive correction before binding: update the worker instructions that still require a human mint and make unattended workers park. Otherwise the CLI becomes headless while the prescribed workflow remains blocked.

All source citations below refer to `65fc6f74abe90c598b05d720d331626c67743dac`. Verification used pinned source reads only; no tests, edits, or GitHub writes.

## Answers to the seven questions

1. **What does R1 lose?** It removes an attended checkpoint on the supported CLI path, but I found no durable proof of that checkpoint in these records. The shared stamp check examines strings. The one-PR mint proof consumes approved-scope and retains its separate human-stamp check (`packages/core/src/policy/one-pr-scope-proof.ts:294–299`). Merge-base and contract checks remain useful even without human approval.

2. **Stamp choice?** Use `declared`, accepted locally by both parsers **and builders**. Keep legacy records readable and leave `isHumanApprovalStamp` unchanged. Permit agent identity in declaration attribution; do not require an agent to supply a human-looking actor. Continuing to emit human stamps would preserve misleading provenance.

3. **Are retained stores protected?** They have meaningful hook restrictions on covered paths and tools, not an authenticated human-only boundary. Keep their mints as defense in depth. The table must qualify worktree-root coverage, unobserved tools, forge writes, and terminal/environment assumptions. Do not claim every `git checkout` or absolute main-clone write is denied without tracing that path.

4. **Start and revoke?** Keep them unchanged in this slice. Tightening authorization can still disrupt another worker or campaign. Their rationale is operator control over shared authorization state, not prevention of self-approval.

5. **UAT refusal?** Keep it. Removing the terminal checkpoint does not require changing campaign freeze semantics.

6. **New gates or reads?** R1–R6 require no new network read or default refusal. Ship the two verbs, cohort handling, local stamp acceptance, worker instructions, remediation, and focused tests together. Defer stronger signatures and hook-gap repairs.

7. **Earlier contracts?** Explicitly supersede the mandatory attended-ask and unattended-park requirements for these two declarations. Amend the described #6945 fallback premise accordingly. I verified the existing #5010-derived worker instructions at the pin; #6945’s full thread was not supplied, so its precise amendment needs parent verification.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — CLI removal alone leaves the unattended stop intact

**Evidence:** `content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md:537–541` requires an attended ask, parks unattended hard facts, forbids agent-shell mint commands, and prohibits parent auto-approval. `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:28–31` repeats those requirements in worker dispatch instructions.

**Failure mode:** A compliant headless worker still parks after R1–R6. Another worker follows the new command documentation and contradicts its dispatch instructions. The proposed removal therefore does not reliably relieve P1.

**Disposition:** Extend R5 beyond terminal remediation. Explicitly replace these requirements with declaration creation and prior landing for the two affected record types, including their swarm instruction copies. Preserve the existing invariant/fail-fast guidance and merge-base checks. Do not silently reinterpret a declaration as human consent.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Declaration acceptance must cover construction and identity

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/observable-scope/mint.ts:224–229` and `packages/core/src/intent-constraint/mint.ts:151–156` reject nonhuman stamps during construction. The cohort uses these builders (`packages/runtime/src/scope-record-cohort.ts:132–143,176–185`). The shared predicate rejects actors `agent`, `agent:*`, and `self` (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/digest.ts:235–251`).

**Failure mode:** Parser-only acceptance leaves newly declared records unwritable. Reusing the human actor restriction would encourage automated writers to impersonate an operator in display metadata.

**Disposition:** Make R2 explicitly cover both builders and parsers. New CLI output always carries `declared`; attribution may honestly identify an agent. Test the record round trip with an agent actor, alongside legacy acceptance and rejection by the unchanged global human predicate. This completes the proposed mechanism without adding a gate.

### 3. sharpens-framing — “Protected” must name its enforcement boundary

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/authz/evaluate.ts:329–335` resolves protection against the worktree or project root. `packages/core/src/authz/protected-dest-realpath.ts:35–39` excludes outside-root writes from that helper. `packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts:41–49` lists covered shell tools without PowerShell. The mint checks environment markers and terminal interactions (`packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts:305–318,320–362`), rather than a signed operator identity.

**Disposition:** Keep R4, but describe retained mints as restrictions on supported CLI and hook-observed paths. Mark main-clone absolute-path and Git-mediated writes as coverage-dependent unless independently verified. Repairs remain outside this slice; the table must not imply those repairs already exist.

### 4. footnote — Preserve the useful part of the declaration model

The merge-base requirement still separates prior declaration from product changes. I prefer this narrow declaration model over protecting two more stores. The strongest case for retaining attended approval is preserving independent judgment over new behavior. That would change my verdict if a consumer verified independent approval; the checked string stamps do not supply it.

The split is right, and the premise holds. An agent can already write an observable-scope or intent-constraint record by hand, and every reader accepts it. So the terminal step on those two verbs stops only an agent that chooses to obey it. The lean can bind. Five things must change first:

- The rule for which mints to keep is stated wrong. The real test is not "do hooks guard the folder". It is "is the record read as authority before anyone merges a PR".
- The worker preamble and the skills still tell workers to park and wait for a human mint. If they are not recut, a headless swarm still stops.
- The verb must not take a human-looking `--kind` or `--actor` from an agent shell.
- The docs must say plainly that after the change, a story fact found mid-build still needs a merged PR before the product PR, and in bot-merge repos no human sees it.

## Answers to the seven questions

1. **Refutation target.** It survives, with one limit. No reader treats these records as approval beyond a shape check. The readers are the two parsers (`observable-scope/mint.ts` 150, `intent-constraint/mint.ts` 102), the two evaluators, `presentation-coverage/admission.ts` 130, and `pr-closing-keywords/brief-land-records.ts` 111. Their only stamp check is `isHumanApprovalStamp` (`scope-provenance/digest.ts` 232-252), which checks the shape of two strings. The code says this itself (`scope-record-cohort.ts` 11, 601; `brief-land-records.ts` 11-12). What R1 does lose: (a) the stop for an agent that obeys the gate, which is the only time a human touches the record when the merge is not human (finding 4), and (b) the cohort form's printed record set before the typed `mint` (`scope-record-cohort.ts` 590-603), which is a weak review moment, not proof of review.
2. **Stamp.** Use `declared`, accepted by these two parsers only. Do not keep today's stamp without the TTY step: an agent-run verb would then write a human-looking stamp, which is worse than a hand-written one. Accepting `declared` loosens nothing real. The shape check never authenticated anything, it only rejected honest `agent` or `self` labels. R2 is incomplete, though (finding 3).

5. **UAT refusal on the dropped verbs.** Keep it. It is an existing refusal, it costs nothing outside UAT, and a hand-write during UAT is already denied by the UAT lease.

## In plain English

Problem: `scope:record-observable-scope` and `scope:record-intent-constraint` stop until a person types `mint` at a real terminal. That stop proves someone was at a terminal, not that anyone reviewed the record, and an agent can already write the same record by hand because the checks look only at the stamp's shape. Consumers pay a stop per story or cohort, worker instructions tell unattended workers to park for that mint, and no single list says which mints still guard something.

Accepted solution: the two commands write their records from any shell with no terminal step, single path and cohort form. They always write a `declared` stamp naming the command and refuse `--kind` and `--minted-via`; the actor is an optional declared-by name that may be an agent. Both builders and both parsers accept `declared` while the shared human-stamp check stays closed, so a declared record never counts as human approval for approved-scope, the one-PR proof or any other reader. The reader ships with the writer. The UAT refusal stays. Every `authz:*` command and template (including `uat-start`, `uat-suspend`, `revoke` and `one-pr-unit`) and `scope:record-approved-scope` keep the mint, because their records are live authority inside the session before any PR exists. One table in `content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md` lists every mint, where its record is read, what it prevents, what a kept mint buys and its named limits.

Limits accepted: a declared record is a declaration the product check holds the PR to, not an approval. Under human merge, the human stop moves from the terminal to the merge that lands the record; under bot merge or a merge under the operator's identity, nothing human checks it. A fact found mid-build still needs a record PR before the product PR. A kept mint buys a command that stops while agent markers are set, plus the in-checkout write deny for `.deft/authz/` and `.deft/approved-scope/`; it does not make a store unwritable (PowerShell tool, absolute writes from a linked worktree into the main clone's grant store, forge commits). ## Problem

Every operator mint goes through `refuseNonInteractiveMint` (`packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts`): a real TTY, no agent or CI markers, `--confirm`, and a typed `mint`. That proves a human is present, not that the human reviewed anything. For some verbs it is the only thing standing between an agent and a self-approval, because the record lands in a store the hooks protect (`.deft/authz/`, `.deft/approved-scope/`). For others it protects nothing: the #6937 triage found that `.deft/observable-scope/` and `.deft/intent-constraint/` are not hook-protected and `isHumanApprovalStamp` checks stamp shape only, so an agent can write those records by hand and the terminal step is pure cost. Consumers hit these mints repeatedly and cannot leave a headless swarm running (deftai/evolution reports, #6937, #7011-era feedback).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An inventory lists every verb that calls `refuseNonInteractiveMint`, with the store it writes, whether hooks protect that store, and what self-approval it prevents.
- [ ] Each verb whose record lands in an unprotected store either drops the TTY step (record written by the agent, with the human merge of the PR that lands it as the stated control) or has its store added to the protected set, with the choice justified per verb.
- [ ] Verbs whose records land in a protected store keep the TTY mint until a stronger approval exists (#6945).
- [ ] Docs list which actions still need an operator mint and why, in one table.
- [ ] Tests cover one dropped-mint verb writing its record without a TTY and one kept-mint verb still refusing without a TTY.

Refs #6937, #6945, #6284, #3156, #5010.
